holidays.name: National Cheeseburger Day
holidays.description: A day devoted to the glory of the cheeseburger, when diners everywhere chase deals, discounts, and the perfect melt. Toppings debates are practically mandatory.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial American food holiday that gained traction in the 2010s, with restaurant chains promoting deals each year. It is not an official government observance.
holidays.funFact: Melted cheese on a burger is often credited to a 1920s California cook, though several American restaurateurs claim to have invented the cheeseburger.

holidays.name: International Read an eBook Day
holidays.description: A celebration of digital reading, inviting people to download a book and finish a chapter without ever touching a paper page. It is a great excuse to carry a whole library in your pocket.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance created to promote e-books and digital reading, tied to the rise of e-readers and reading apps.
holidays.funFact: Project Gutenberg, started in 1971 by Michael Hart, is often cited as the first e-book effort, which makes e-books older than the World Wide Web.

holidays.name: National Play-Doh Day
holidays.description: A day to squish, roll, and sculpt with the world's most famous modeling compound. Adults are officially allowed to join in and pretend it is stress relief.
holidays.origin: Play-Doh began in the 1930s as a wallpaper cleaner and was later reformulated and marketed as a children's modeling toy in the 1950s. The day is an informal toy celebration.
holidays.funFact: Play-Doh's original purpose was to clean coal soot off wallpaper, and it became a toy when coal heating declined.

holidays.name: National Respect Day
holidays.description: A day for pausing to treat others with a little more courtesy, kindness, and consideration. Expect extra holding of doors and fewer eye rolls.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial awareness observance promoted by social media and community groups, encouraging people to practice respect in daily life.
holidays.funFact: Many languages have special grammatical forms to show respect, such as formal 'you' pronouns in French, German, and Spanish, as well as honorific speech levels in Japanese and Korean.

holidays.name: World Water Monitoring Day
holidays.description: A day when volunteers test local streams, rivers, and lakes to see how healthy their water really is. It lets ordinary people play scientist with test kits and a bit of mud.
holidays.origin: The observance was started in 2003 by America's Clean Water Foundation to encourage public involvement in protecting water resources, and it has since expanded internationally.
holidays.funFact: Citizen scientists using simple test kits measure things like temperature, acidity, clarity, and dissolved oxygen, and some even use turbidity tubes to check how murky the water is.
